practiceQuestions.q: Which article of the Constitution of India provides for the establishment of the Finance Commission?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 280 of the Constitution of India provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission by the President every fifth year or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary. [Primary Reference: Article 280, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Under which statutory body are the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) constituted?
practiceQuestions.sol: The CBDT and CBIC were bifurcated and constituted under the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963. [Primary Reference: Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963 / Ministry of Finance]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the apex constitutional body that audits all receipts and expenditure of the Government of India, including tax revenues?
opts: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
practiceQuestions.sol: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India, appointed under Article 148, audits all receipts and expenditures of the Union and State governments, including tax revenues. [Primary Reference: Article 148, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: The Goods and Services Tax Council (GST Council) derives its authority from which constitutional article inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 279A, inserted by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, provides for the constitution of the GST Council by the President. [Primary Reference: Article 279A, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairperson of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council in India?
opts: Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 279A, the Union Finance Minister is the Chairperson of the GST Council, and the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance is a member. [Primary Reference: Article 279A(2), Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), functioning under the Ministry of Law and Justice, deals with appeals under which major tax enactment?
practiceQuestions.sol: ITAT is a statutory body established under Section 252 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, dealing with appeals under direct taxes. [Primary Reference: Section 252, Income Tax Act, 1961]

practiceQuestions.q: Which authority acts as the apex national appellate body for indirect taxes, specifically customs, central excise, and service tax disputes?
opts: Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT)
practiceQuestions.sol: CESTAT is a statutory tribunal established under Section 129C of the Customs Act, 1962, to hear appeals against orders passed by the Commissioner of Customs or Central Excise. [Primary Reference: Section 129C, Customs Act, 1962]

practiceQuestions.q: The National Anti-profiteering Authority (NAA) was originally established under the provisions of which tax legislation?
opts: Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Act, 2017
practiceQuestions.sol: NAA was established under Rule 127 of the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Rules, 2017, framed under the CGST Act, 2017. [Primary Reference: CGST Rules, 2017 / Ministry of Finance]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary mandate of the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)?
opts: Formulation of policies relating to direct taxes and administration of direct tax laws
Levying and collecting customs duties and GST
Auditing all government accounts and tax revenues
practiceQuestions.sol: CBDT deals with matters relating to the levy and collection of direct taxes (Income Tax, Corporation Tax, etc.) and formulates policies through the Department of Revenue. [Primary Reference: Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963]

practiceQuestions.q: Which institution handles intelligence, investigation, and enforcement against tax evasion, money laundering, and foreign exchange violations in India?
opts: Securities and Exchange Board of India
practiceQuestions.sol: The Enforcement Directorate (ED), under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, enforces PMLA, FEMA, and fugitive economic offenders acts. [Primary Reference: Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance]

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Finance Commission ensure fiscal federalism balance between the Union and the States through institutional mechanisms?
opts: By directly setting tax rates for individual state goods and services
By recommending the horizontal and vertical devolution of net proceeds of taxes from the divisible pool
By auditing state treasury expenditures on a monthly basis
